title: 2007 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: Point \(P\) is inside equilateral \(\triangle ABC.\) Points \(Q,\) \(R,\) and \(S\) are the feet of the perpendiculars from \(P\) to \(\overline{AB},\) \(\overline{BC},\) and \(\overline{CA},\) respectively. Given that \(PQ=1,\) \(PR=2,\) and \(PS=3,\) what is \(AB?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(s=AB.\) Joining \(P\) to the vertices splits the triangle into \(\triangle PAB,\) \(\triangle PBC,\) and \(\triangle PCA,\) with areas \(\tfrac{s}{2},\) \(s,\) and \(\tfrac{3s}{2}.\)

Their total is \(3s,\) which must equal the area \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2\) of the equilateral triangle. So \[ 3s=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2, \] giving \(s=\dfrac{12}{\sqrt3}=4\sqrt3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Split \(\triangle ABC\) into \(\triangle PAB,\) \(\triangle PBC,\) \(\triangle PCA,\) using the perpendiculars as heights
Their areas sum to \(\tfrac12 s(1+2+3),\) which also equals \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2\)
